guidance: Excess rainfall can lead to crop lodging, flower/grain shedding, or root suffocation. Timely intimation to your local agricultural office or insurance representative may be required depending on the applicable scheme or insurer rules.
information_to_collect: Approximate date, start time, and duration of the heavy rainfall event
Affected crop type, variety, and stage of growth (e.g. flowering, grain filling, maturity)
Estimated land area affected in acres or hectares
Visible physical symptoms (e.g. lodged stems, waterlogging, washed away topsoil)
useful_evidence: Clear daylight photographs showing the extent of flattened or water-damaged crops
Wide-angle panoramic field photograph showing field boundaries and standing water
Local weather report or newspaper clipping noting the excessive precipitation event, if available
general_next_steps: Check whether safe surface drainage can be opened without disturbing root systems further
Record the incident date and notify your village agriculture officer (AEO/VAA) or insurer helpline as early as possible
Keep land records (Pattadar Passbook / RoR) and insurance premium deduction receipt ready for inspection

guidance: Submergence and prolonged standing water deprive roots of oxygen and can cause extensive root rot or silt suffocation. In many notified schemes, localized inundation post-sowing may be considered for assessment, subject to official surveyor verification.
information_to_collect: Date and approximate time when floodwater or runoff entered the field parcel
Depth of standing water and continuous number of days the crop has remained submerged
Crop type, sown acreage, and approximate percentage of area submerged
Source of inundation (e.g. river overflow, canal breach, heavy localized surface runoff)
useful_evidence: Close-up photographs of submerged foliage, silt deposition, or rotting lower stems
Panoramic shots establishing recognizable landmarks (electric pole, well, access road) for location verification
Dated photographs taken on consecutive days showing duration of water stagnation
general_next_steps: Prioritize personal and family safety before entering flooded agricultural areas
Intimate your local agriculture office, Gram Panchayat, or insurer toll-free channel promptly
Do not plow under or prematurely clear the damaged crop until official inspection is completed or advised

guidance: Prolonged dry spells during critical growth stages cause moisture stress, stunted growth, and permanent wilting. Insurance assistance for widespread drought is generally evaluated at the area unit level based on seasonal rainfall indices or crop cutting experiments, depending on scheme notifications.
information_to_collect: Duration of the dry spell (number of continuous weeks without rainfall or irrigation)
Current growth stage of the crop (vegetative, flowering, pod/grain development)
Soil type and primary irrigation status (rainfed, borewell, canal availability)
Observed symptoms (permanent wilting, leaf scorching, stunted height, failure to flower)
useful_evidence: Photographs showing severe soil cracking and withered or scorched plants
Comparison photos of affected field sections versus any irrigated reference patch
Local rain-gauge, mandal, or block-level deficit rainfall advisories if available
general_next_steps: Adopt moisture conservation practices (mulching, light hoeing) where feasible
Check whether your mandal or block is officially notified as drought-affected by the state government
Consult your village agriculture assistant or local cooperative society regarding area-wide assessment schedules

guidance: Hailstones cause sudden, severe mechanical injury including shredded leaves, broken stems, bruised fruits, and fallen flowers. Hailstorm is widely treated as a localized calamity under major crop insurance guidelines, requiring prompt notification.
information_to_collect: Exact date and time of the hailstorm event
Duration of the hail event and approximate size of hailstones (e.g. marble-sized, lemon-sized)
Specific crop parts damaged (foliage, branches, flowers, developing fruits/pods)
Estimated percentage of total crop yield lost across the survey number
useful_evidence: Immediate photographs showing hailstones accumulated on the field surface before melting
Close-up photographs of punctured leaves, broken stalks, bruised fruits, or stripped stems
A reference object (such as a coin or hand) placed next to hailstones or leaf punctures
general_next_steps: Capture photographs as quickly as possible before hailstones melt and wound margins discolor
Notify your local agriculture officer, insurance company helpline, or bank without delay
Consult an agriculture extension officer for prophylactic sprays to prevent secondary fungal entry through physical wounds

guidance: High-velocity winds and cyclonic squalls can uproot standing crops, cause severe lodging (flattening), or snap fruit-bearing branches. Eligibility and coverage for localized wind damage depend on local scheme notifications and event classification.
information_to_collect: Date, time, and duration of the storm or gale-force wind event
Crop height, growth stage, and whether the crop is completely lodged or tilted
Extent of uprooting versus stem bending or breakage
Whether the windstorm was accompanied by intense rainfall
useful_evidence: Photographs capturing the direction and pattern of lodged plant rows across the plot
Close-up photos of snapped stems, torn canopies, or exposed roots
Wide landscape view showing the scale of the damage across adjoining farm boundaries
general_next_steps: Avoid attempting to mechanically straighten severely lodged mature plants without expert advice, as brittle stems may snap
Report the incident to the village revenue officer, agriculture extension officer, or insurer channel
Prepare your land survey and khata details in advance for the surveyor's joint field inspection

topic: Pest Attack and Crop Disease Damage
guidance: Severe pest outbreaks and disease epidemics can cause widespread yield reduction. Coverage for pest and disease attacks is typically evaluated at the area unit level based on seasonal crop cutting experiments, though specific provisions can vary across schemes.
information_to_collect: Type of pest or symptom observed (e.g. brown planthopper, stem borer holes, fungal blight, viral curling)
Approximate date when the infestation first became noticeable
Previous plant protection measures, spray dates, and chemicals applied
Proportion of total crop area exhibiting severe damage
useful_evidence: Clear close-up photos of active insect pests, larvae, egg masses, or distinct foliar lesions
Photographs showing both healthy and severely affected patches side by side
Purchase receipts for recommended agrochemical inputs applied, if available
general_next_steps: Consult the local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or Agriculture Extension Officer immediately for management advisory
Check whether an area-wide epidemic notification has been issued for your mandal or district
Keep your sowing verification and input purchase documentation organized for potential inquiry
